title: Infleqtion Reports Q2 2026 Results: Record Revenue Up 116% YoY, Raised Guidance to $43M, and $100M CHIPS Act LOI - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ) posted record Q2 2026 revenue of $12.63M, up 116% YoY and 33.5% sequentially, all organic, and raised FY2026 guidance to ~$43M — while the U.S. Commerce Department signed a $100M CHIPS Act LOI that contemplates the government taking common stock, and NASA gravity gradiometry, not quantum computing, was the primary revenue driver.

insights.claim: Infleqtion generated record Q2 2026 revenue of $12.63 million, up 116.3% year-over-year from $5.84M and 33.5% sequentially from $9.46M, with growth entirely organic.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Infleqtion is currently the higher-revenue, faster-sequencing quantum pure-play versus Quantinuum's $8.00M quarter — the comparison matters for relative sector positioning.
insights.quote: Top-line expansion was entirely organic and derived 100% from quantum hardware, software, and sensing deployments.

insights.claim: Infleqtion raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $43 million, which implies roughly $20.9M of second-half revenue against $22.09M already booked in the first half — an implied sequential flattening.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The raised guide is less aggressive than it looks: it implies H2 revenue below H1, so a beat is plausible but the framing may be deliberately conservative.
insights.quote: Infleqtion raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to approximately $43 million.

insights.claim: Infleqtion's Q2 operating expenses of $32.49M skewed toward SG&A at $19.82M versus only $12.68M of R&D, offset by $0.47M grant income.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: SG&A running 56% above R&D at a deep-tech company suggests heavy go-to-market and public-company cost build; watch whether that ratio inverts as revenue scales.
insights.locator: Operating expenses for the quarter totaled

insights.claim: Infleqtion's GAAP net loss narrowed 15.8% sequentially to ($25.47M), or ($0.12) per share, with non-GAAP loss from operations of ($16.98M) after excluding $12.07M of stock-based compensation and transaction expenses.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sequential loss improvement alongside 33.5% revenue growth is the operating-leverage signal bulls need; one more quarter of it would change the burn trajectory narrative.

insights.claim: Infleqtion holds $476.96M in cash and short-term investments, and $582.0 million in total liquid capital reserves including non-current securities and restricted cash, with zero debt.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Zero debt plus ~$582M of liquidity against a ~$25M quarterly loss gives roughly five years of runway — financing risk is off the table through the 2027 Illinois deployment.
insights.quote: Adding non-current securities ($104.78M) and restricted cash brings total liquid capital reserves to $582.0 million (zero debt).

insights.claim: Infleqtion's Q2 cash balance includes a temporary $27.4 million working-capital benefit from collected stock option payroll taxes that are remitted in Q3, overstating the true quarter-end cash position.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Adjust Q3 expectations down by $27.4M of cash outflow that has nothing to do with operations, or the sequential cash burn will look alarming.
insights.quote: Q2 balance includes a temporary $27.4 million working-capital benefit from collected stock option payroll taxes remitted in Q3.

insights.claim: The U.S. Department of Commerce selected Infleqtion for a Letter of Intent providing up to $100 million in proposed CHIPS Act funding after a technical review of the company's hardware roadmap.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $100M LOI is over twice the company's full-year revenue guide — non-dilutive-scale capital that de-risks the neutral-atom roadmap, though it is an LOI, not cash received.

insights.claim: The proposed CHIPS Act funding contemplates the U.S. Department of Commerce receiving common stock in Infleqtion, converting an industrial policy grant into a government equity position in a listed company.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government equity stakes in strategic tech are becoming a policy template — it dilutes holders and injects political risk into the cap table, a factor equity models rarely price.
insights.quote: The proposed funding contemplates the Department of Commerce receiving common stock in Infleqtion.

insights.claim: Infleqtion was selected for three U.S. Department of Energy Genesis Mission projects spanning AI, nuclear applications and fusion research, deepening its federal revenue concentration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Federal program wins are sticky and high-margin but expose the equity to appropriations cycles and administration priorities.

insights.claim: Infleqtion CEO Matt Kinsella testified before the U.S. House Committee on Natural Resources on the Quantum-Enhanced Critical Minerals Mapping Act of 2026, tying quantum sensing to critical minerals policy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum sensing is being bundled into the critical-minerals and resource-security agenda — a legislative channel that could create a mandated demand pool.

insights.claim: Infleqtion is on track to demonstrate 30 logical qubits in 2026, with defined circuits for enterprise customer workloads across energy, finance and precision medicine.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 30-logical-qubit demo this calendar year is the binary technical catalyst for INFQ; missing it would undercut the entire raised-guidance narrative.
insights.quote: On track to demonstrate 30 logical qubits in 2026, with defined circuits for enterprise customer workloads across energy, finance, and precision medicine.

insights.claim: Infleqtion is under contract to deploy a neutral-atom quantum computer at the Illinois Quantum & Microelectronics Park in 2027 using a modular architecture designed to scale past 50 logical qubits toward a long-term goal of 100.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A contracted 2027 installation converts roadmap into backlog; modularity is the claimed path from 30 to 100 logical qubits without a new physics breakthrough.
insights.quote: The system features a new modular architecture designed to scale past 50 logical qubits toward a long-term goal of 100 logical qubits.

insights.claim: Eaton is using private-cloud access to Infleqtion's Sqale system for complex energy grid applications, giving Infleqtion a named industrial enterprise customer in the power sector.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A named Fortune 500 industrial paying for private-cloud QPU access is rarer than partnership announcements; grid optimization may be the first commercial quantum vertical to convert.

insights.claim: Infleqtion appointed Dr. Joseph Buck, a former Lockheed Martin Senior Fellow, as Senior Vice President of Quantum Computing Systems to lead Sqale development.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hiring defense-primes engineering leadership signals Infleqtion is building for government systems delivery discipline, consistent with its federal revenue mix.

themes.theme: Sensing is the actual revenue engine

insights.claim: Execution on NASA's quantum gravity gradiometer program was a primary revenue driver in Q2, meaning Infleqtion's record quarter was carried by quantum sensing rather than quantum computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: INFQ is priced as a quantum computing story but monetizes as a sensing and metrology contractor — the two verticals carry very different multiples and risk profiles.
insights.quote: Execution on NASA’s gravity gradiometry program served as a primary revenue driver in Q2.

insights.claim: Infleqtion is commercializing third-generation Tiqker optical atomic clocks through a global co-selling partnership with Safran.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Safran distribution puts atomic clocks into aerospace and GNSS-denied navigation channels — a near-term, deployable product line while computing stays pre-revenue at scale.

insights.claim: Infleqtion runs dual computing and sensing verticals, a structure that lets sensing contracts fund the longer-dated neutral-atom computing roadmap.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Dual-vertical quantum companies self-fund their compute R&D from sensing cash flow, a structurally lower-risk model than pure-play computing bets.
insights.quote: record quarterly performance driven by 100% organic growth across its dual computing and sensing verticals
